title: Sequence Sets the Extent and the Nature of the Conformational Response of the Engrailed Homeodomain to DNA
content: Homeodomains, the DNA-binding domains of eukaryotic transcription factors directing developmental programs, all bind very similar TAAT-based sequences, yet the factors carrying them regulate hundreds of genes. We showed previously that the engrailed homeodomain uses a promiscuous recognition code that grades DNA along a ladder of affinities, and that it changes conformation on binding its cognate motif, in a transition released by a built-in electrostatic spring-loaded latch. Whether the latch is reserved for cognate signals was untested. Here, by NMR and circular dichroism, we compare the responses of domain and DNA at both ends of that ladder: the cognate duplex and a duplex designed with minimal cognate similarity. We find that the latch releases on non-cognate DNA, in a pattern consistent with conformational rheostat operation. The domain also stiffens both duplexes without reshaping them, by an amount scaled with the association strength. Amide chemical shifts indicate that the non-cognate complex is distinct, with the interface held through charge, only part of the base reading segment retained, the C-terminal end of helix 3 unstructured, and the core repacked in the opposite direction. Sequence thus sets the extent and nature of the protein response, which could let a promiscuous factor scan without stalling while remaining localized at its regulatory regions.
